To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have generated amphotropic retroviral vectors that exhibit strong protection from human complement attack by fusion of the catalytic region of DAF to the EnvA protein.

the catalytic domain from the human complement regulatory molecule, DAF, when expressed as a fusion protein with the envelope protein of amphotropic MuLV, results in a virus that is protected from human complement attack.
the fusion protein DAFF/4070A protects retroviruses from human serum in vitro and in vivo.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a new method for generating retrovirus-based gene therapy vectors that exhibit protection against human complement.
the development of a novel gene therapy vector for the treatment of inherited diseases in humans.
the development of an amphotropic retrovirus vector that is protected against human complement.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the use of the human complement regulator DAF is the only one of the three tested human CRPs which can protect retroviral vectors from human serum.
the DAFF2A fusion protein is a promising candidate for the protection of murine retrovirus-based vectors against complement attack in human serum.
DAFF2A retroviral vectors are protected against human complement attack and are suitable for human gene transfer.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the complement regulatory protein DAF can be successfully used for protection of retroviruses against human serum.
we have generated a novel retrovirus that is protected against human complement attack.
we have generated a retroviral vector that is protected against human complement attack and that is suitable for human in vivo retroviral gene transfer.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the membrane of murine retrovirus can be modified by the fusion of human complement regulatory proteins.
the fusion of a human complement regulatory protein to a retroviral envelope protein is an efficient strategy for generating retroviruses with strong complement protection.

the fusion of the catalytic domains of complement regulatory proteins to the envelope protein of amphotropic murin leukemia viruses results in complement-protected retroviruses that are suitable for gene therapy in humans.
